title: Flat input models and the specified etale open coefficient-counit equation
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion of separated finite-type $k$-schemes [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings annihilated by powers of $\ell$. Write $\mathcal C^t_{T,R}=D^b_{ctf}(T_t,R)$ for the full subcategory of the ordinary constant-$R$ module derived category with bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude, where $t=e,p$ denotes the small etale or pro-etale site: tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf has cohomology in a fixed finite interval [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf, def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Write $C_T^R=\nu_T^*$ for exact site comparison, $T_T^t=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$, $J_R^t=Dj_{!,R}^t$, and $U_R^t=j_R^{t,*}$ for exact restriction [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism, det-sp-scalar-extension-functor, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image].
The functors $J_R^t,U_R^t$ and $T_T^t$ preserve these finite-Tor constructible subcategories for $R=A,B$, and $C_T^R$ gives equivalences between them. Every $M\in\mathcal C^p_{X,A}$ is isomorphic to $C_X^AK$ with $K\in\mathcal C^e_{X,A}$. If $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, it has a representative $P$, zero outside $[a,b]$, whose terms are flat constructible sheaves. The restricted complex $U_A^eP$, the extended complex $J_A^eU_A^eP$, their site pullbacks, and their ordinary scalar extensions to $B$ are bounded K-flat complexes with flat terms, computing the corresponding derived operations [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex].
Let $v_R^e:J_R^eU_R^e\to1$ be the actual degreewise evaluation counit, given by $s\mapsto s$ on each extension summand and zero on an empty summand [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Let $\beta_j:T_X^eJ_A^e\xrightarrow{\sim}J_B^eT_U^e$ be the specified compact-support coefficient map for the identity-proper-factor compactification of $j$ [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], and $a_j^e:T_U^eU_A^e\xrightarrow{\sim}U_B^eT_X^e$ the inverse of the canonical K-flat scalar/pullback comparison [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso]. The specified $\beta_j$ on $P$ is the summandwise tensor comparison. On every $K\in\mathcal C^e_{X,A}$,
$$v_{B,T_X^eK}^e\circ J_B^e(a_{j,K}^e)\circ\beta_j(U_A^eK)=T_X^e(v_{A,K}^e).$$
All these assertions hold without flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$.

source.place: Locality; bounded flat representatives, change of coefficients and evaluation counit

proof.text: For a nonempty Tor interval choose a bounded flat constructible representative by the existing flat-model theorem. For an empty interval testing Tor amplitude against the unit makes the object zero; choose the zero complex. Exact restriction preserves flat terms and constructibility, and quasi-compact open extension preserves them too. The bounded-flat coefficient/site-square theorem, applied on the enlarged interval [min(a,b),b], gives K-flatness and the actual scalar representatives; termwise preservation of zero restores the exact requested support in [a,b]. Apply this to P, j*P and j!j*P.

proof.text: Exact-localization factor isomorphisms identify the restricted and extended complexes with their derived operations. Apply the canonical comparison/pullback and comparison/open-extension isomorphisms to identify both pro-etale operation models. Thus all four operationModels isomorphisms are actual derived isomorphisms.

source.place: Locality; bounded flat representatives, change of coefficients and evaluation counit

proof.text: The proper factor is the identity. Compatibility of right-derived natural isomorphisms with the exact-derived identifications equates the two canonical identity direct-image boundaries. The scalarMate identity law then cancels these boundaries. The properOpenCoefficientOpenInverse is characterized by its adjunction transpose; scalarOpen_unit identifies this transpose with the inverse of openScalarExtension. Hence coefficientMap equals the hom of that specified isomorphism, on every input.

source.place: Locality; bounded flat representatives, change of coefficients and evaluation counit

proof.text: For a bounded flat complex the independent-coefficient K-flat criterion applies after the canonical constant-module realization. The ordinary open restriction/scalar isomorphism is the inverse of the recorded upperStarRestrictScalarsIsoSheaf; therefore the ordinary open scalar isomorphism equals sheafCoefficientIso. The open tensor normalization gives coefficientModelEquation after cancelling the exact-localization factor. The etale sum sheet computation gives sheetEquation, since open and etale sum extension and their adjunctions agree definitionally.

source.place: Locality; bounded flat representatives, change of coefficients and evaluation counit

proof.text: The exact-derived adjunction counit on a localized cochain complex is obtained from the homotopy-category counit and the two exact factor maps. The homotopy counit is the quotient of the degreewise ordinary counit. This is exactly evaluationComplexMap, giving evaluationModelEquation over A and B. Finally the open tensor counit law, with the canonical restriction comparison identified with properOpenCoefficientPullbackIso inverse, yields the required actual coefficient/counit identity for every K.
